chapters.title: Chapter 4665: Surprise II
paragraphs: The Depths held fragments of The Earliest Folds.
When Noah delved into this place before, he had found a number of things, but seeing how the final level held such a thing, he moved faster than Planck Speed as he appeared at the end of the wall.

At the end of a multicolored wall that pulsed with ancient authority, there was a humanoid entity who seemed to be getting pulled into the wall itself. Multicolored chains were stuck into his body at various points, connecting back to this wall like roots drawing sustenance from soil. Each chain pulsed with its own frequency, its own color, its own terrible purpose.

A faint glimmer ofTHE Civilizational Authority of Existencecould be felt on the walls and chains as the one bound by them seemed to be in a state of slumber, his head drooped forward and his body hanging limply like a puppet whose strings had been cut but whose frame remained suspended.
Noah’s eyes blazed with immensity and brilliance as the weight of an entity atTHE Intermediate Depth of Absolute Sovereigntyerupted from him.
He opened his eyes fully and radiated a brilliant flash of blue-gold light that shockingly released a Logos, one that closely meant "Break what is unbreakable."
HUUM!

The chains of Existence binding this entity down shattered one after another in a cascade of multicolored fragments that dissolved into nothing before they even hit the ground. Each chain snapped with a sound like reality itself crying out in protest, but Noah’s authority was absolute and his command was undeniable.
Noah then appeared beside this entity who was about to fall and placed his hands around his shoulders as he slowly began to carry them from their chained location toward the center of this place.

All around them, waves of multicolored radiance permeated the space as if the cavern itself was responding to the breaking of those ancient chains. And as he moved, the entity he supported began to flutter his eyes wide open before they focused on him, and a look of shock and recognition bloomed across his features.
Then this entity smiled weakly and said, "Haha, friend, what in the unfathomable Weavings of Existence brought you here?"
Noah looked back at this being as he brought him down to the center of this place, gazing at the weakened body of an entity he had met as a brilliant man long ago.
"I need to ask the same of you, Anaximander,"Noah replied with genuine curiosity mixed with concern. "How exactly did you come to be here?"
BOOM!
Yes, it was Anaximander, the brilliant Fold Dweller he had met in The Earliest Folds!

He looked unfathomably weak as his figure even seemed illusory at some points, as if he was here and not here at the same time. His dark hair was now mixed with streaks of white that hadn’t been there before, and he was adorned in a simple white robe at this moment that hung loosely on his diminished frame. But his eyes still held that same brilliance that seemed to be thinking of countless things in one instant, that spark of endless curiosity that defined his very existence.
Noah looked at him and shook his head at the state this once vibrant entity had been reduced to.
Anaximander smiled while sighing as he began to stretch and look around at the cavern that had been his prison.

"Too many things have happened,"Anaximander said with a voice that held both exhaustion and a strange sense of acceptance."I never expected that one of the parts of me laid out across Existence would be discovered by you of all beings."
Noah’s brows rose at these words. "One of the parts of your existence? There are many others out there?"

Anaximander smiled and shook his head before he replied, "There were many others scattered across the Folds and hidden in places that even THE entities would struggle to find. They have either been lost through time or right now since one of me has awakened, they will all return to their source."
He paused, and a light returned to Anaximander’s eyes slowly as he looked at Noah with an apologetic expression that held genuine remorse.

"I heard you call me not too long ago," he said quietly. "I heard your words of ’Anaximander, come!’ echoing through the Weavings of Existence itself. I am sorry that I wasn’t able to come to your aid when you needed me. It seems that I got myself mixed up in things that I had no business in, and I paid the price for it even though you had warned me aboutTHEExistences."
His words were heavy ones as Noah sat opposite him, processing everything he was hearing.

Nearby, the figure of Malphas ridiculously brought down a golden plate between them that had silver cups which shone with liquid that could be none other than the Sacred Mead of Existence, as if he were simply a butler serving his master and a friend during a casual afternoon visit rather than in the hundredth level of an excavation depth that held fragments of collapsed reality.
Noah took the cup and drank while staring intently at the entity opposite him who smiled and did the same before he spoke with tiredness that seemed to reach into his very soul.

"I was always curious," Anaximander began, his eyes growing distant as he recalled events that clearly still haunted him. "My mind is that of a scientist, and I always questioned everything around me. To pay back the favor ofTHE Weaversfor showing me the Way, they told me I had to do something simple. All I had to do was go into a place and deliver to them an object. It seemed simple and harmless enough."
He paused and took another sip of the Sacred Mead before continuing.

"Of course, I should have known that this object was not theirs. I should have known that it belonged to another. Nobody had a chance to get this item because it was protected by authorities that would destroy anything that approached. But my Way... my Way did not even need power to bypass such things."
His expression grew more troubled as the memories surfaced.

"I felt immense resistance for the first time ever, and so I simply said... ’There is no resistance in this place that can stop me.’ And when I stood before the object and it seemed far too heavy for anyone to carry, I simply said ’This is something that I can carry.’ It drained everything that I had, but I wanted to repay the favor and get back to studying Existence. So I took the object, and I delivered it toTHE Weavers."
Anaximander’s voice dropped to something barely above a whisper.
"The object I took... belonged toTHE Creature. And it was something truly heavy asTHE Weaversand their master,THE Living Paradox... utilized it to strike againstTHE Heart of THE Creature."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4666: Zero I
paragraphs: Noah’s eyes became immensely sharp as he paid even more attention to Anaximander, the implications of these words sending his mind racing through countless possibilities and connections.
Anaximander looked saddened as he sighed with a sense of guilt that seemed to have been eating at him for eons.

"You cannot imagine the sense of guilt I felt," he continued, his voice heavy with regret that time had done nothing to diminish. "Because to me at that time, I had already metTHE Creature. THE Creaturewas... a friend who had shown me kindness and curiosity about my unique nature. And I had effectively and unknowingly betrayed a friend by delivering the very weapon that would be used to wound him in ways that even now I do not fully understand."
THE Living Paradoxhad actually used Anaximander as a weapon againstTHE Creature.

The way this was done was intricate and unique in itself as Noah found himself questioning howTHE Weavershad known and realized the power that Anaximander held. How did they know he could do what he could do? And that it could even work to take something that belonged toTHE Creature,which was terrifying enough that it could be used to harm him?
There were far too many questions swirling in his mind, but Noah had to start somewhere.
"When did you meet THE Creature?" he asked.
Anaximander smiled at the question as memories of simpler times seemed to flicker across his brilliant eyes.

"It was actually not too long after I met you," he replied with a hint of nostalgia in his voice. "After we parted ways on that snowy landscape in the Earliest Folds, I made my existence seek out someone that could answer my curiosities and questions about the nature of reality itself. And I was led naturally toTHE Creature, as if Existence itself knew that he was the one who could satisfy my endless hunger for understanding."
He looked at Noah with an expression that held both fondness and regret.

"THE Creaturewas even curious and asking me about you when I told him I had made another friend before him," Anaximander continued. "But at that time you told me not to spread your name and Weavings, so I held my mouth and simply described you as an interesting entity I had encountered in my travels."
Noah’s eyes turned sharp at these words.

Because this in itself was unique as even beforeTHE Creaturehad met Anaximander, he had personally gazed at Noah way before The Earliest Folds in Ginnungagap whereTHE Creaturehad saved him from the hands ofTHE Living Temporal. SoTHE Creaturehad always known about him, or at least a glimpse of his figure when he intervened in that moment of crisis. He simply did not know that Noah was the same one that Anaximander was talking about when he mentioned his new friend.
IfTHE Creaturehad known that Noah was in the Earliest Folds at that time, would Noah have gotten another visitor?

The possibilities were many and the implications even greater, but Noah shook his head and focused back on Anaximander before he said, "A lot has happened since then, and I don’t know how much you know. But THE Living Paradox suppressed the Existence of THE Creature and built a weapon called THE Loom, a weapon that he will set off anytime within the next few hours or a few days to bring about an endless and catastrophic storm that will lay waste across Existence. Do you remember when I asked you in the Earliest Folds how to overcome such an ordeal?"
Anaximander smiled with nostalgia at the memory, his eyes lighting up with that familiar spark of intellectual delight.
"Haha, I told you to become the storm," he said with genuine warmth in his weakened voice. "My friend, have you succeeded in becoming the storm itself?"
At such words, Noah looked at the features of this entity in front of him before he nodded slowly and said, "Somewhat. But how did you come to be here?"

Anaximander looked around at this place filled with serene multicolored rivers that flowed in patterns that defied conventional physics, his expression growing more somber as he recalled the events that led to his imprisonment.

"Even after finding out about my betrayal,THE Creatureseemingly understood and took me in my weakened state fromTHE Weavers and THE Living Paradox,"Anaximander explained with wonder still evident in his voice despite the suffering he had endured. "My existence itself seems to be hated by them as they sought to destroy me completely after my uses were done, with my Guidelines barely remaining intact asTHE Creaturemoved to secure me before Paradox could finish what he started."
Anaximander’s Guidelines.

The very foundation of his impossible power. Guideline #1: I exist. Guideline #2: I will continue to exist. Guideline #3: My existence cannot be unwillingly altered or ended by the will or authority of another, and any hostile action or intent directed at him would be treated not as an attack but as an interesting but ultimately irrelevant external phenomenon.

These Guidelines allowed Anaximander to simply decide that attacks did not apply to him, that resistance could not stop him, that weight was something he could carry if he declared it so. His power was ridiculous in its simplicity and terrifying in its implications because it meant that the fundamental rules of Existence were merely suggestions to him rather than absolute laws.

If such a power were to grow and mature, if Anaximander were to expand his Guidelines further and further, the potential across Existence was limitless. He could simply declare that he was stronger thanTHEentities and make it so. He could declare thatTHE Loomcould not harm him and walk through The Fallout untouched. He could declare that he wasTHEand becomeTHEthrough sheer assertion of will.
No wonderTHE Living Paradoxwanted him destroyed.
Anaximander continued with a voice that held deep gratitude despite his weakened state.

"THE Creaturedid not need to worry about me given everything else that was happening," he said softly. "But for some reason, Paradox wanted to collapse me completely, andTHE Creaturewanted to save me. To the extent that the weapon I took from him was used against him, and yet he still moved to secure me. To ensure that Paradox would never find me as he battled against them until I could regain the power that made me who I am."
Oh!

chapters.title: Chapter 4667: Zero II
paragraphs: He paused and looked at Noah with eyes that held centuries of gratitude for a being who had shown him kindness when he deserved none.

"I toldTHE Creatureto spread my Weavings out across Existence so that I could hide in fragments until the time was right," Anaximander continued. "I set up new Guidelines to make it possible, declaring that my existence could be divided and scattered without diminishing my core self. When a time in the future came when things settled down, a friend could come and wake me. I thought that friend would beTHE Creaturereturning after his victory, but it turned out to be you."
He smiled with genuine warmth.
"So here we are, Friend."
Here they were.

Noah silently thought about everything he had just learned before he looked at Anaximander closely and asked the question that had been burning in his mind since he first encountered this impossible being.
"What is your Way?"
His Way.

Anaximander smiled at this question as he looked up to the endlessly obsidian ceiling above them, his expression one of peaceful contemplation as he considered how to explain something that defied conventional explanation.

"My Way is My Way,"he began with that familiar tone of a scientist trying to describe something beyond normal parameters. "My Way is The Way.THE Creature called it The Way of THE Way when we discussed it during our conversations. I called it just... My Way. The Way of Self."
He looked back at Noah with eyes that held the weight of profound understanding.

"You can call it another name if you wish, but it is simply a relationship between me and Existence," Anaximander continued. "I tell Existence how things should be, and Existence simply needs to listen. That is the Way. That is my Way. I do not fight against reality or bend it through force or authority. I simply inform reality of how things are for me, and reality accepts my declaration as truth."
BOOM!
The Way of THE Way.
The Way of Self.

A power that allowed its wielder to redefine their relationship with Existence itself, to make declarations that reality was obligated to accept, to exist outside the normal parameters that bound evenTHEentities.

Noah looked at Anaximander with new understanding as the pieces fell into place. This was whyTHE Living Paradoxwanted him destroyed so badly. This was whyTHE Creaturemoved to protect him despite the betrayal. This was why such a being had been hidden in fragments across Existence rather than allowed to remain whole.
Anaximander’s Way was a threat to the very order thatTHE Living Paradoxsought to impose through THE Loom and The Fallout.
Because how could you destroy someone who simply declared that they could not be destroyed?
How could you impose your will on someone who had already declared that external wills did not apply to them?
How could you win against someone who had decided that they had already won?
It was an absurd Way, and even with it, that bum, Paradox, had still won against it and Existence itself in their first clash.
Noah frowned as he thought about all of it!
As Noah thought about many things, Anaximander in front of him smiled as this being began to rise up on unsteady legs that grew stronger with each passing moment.

"I am an explorer," Anaximander said with that familiar tone of someone who had spent their entire existence chasing understanding. "I am a scientist. I questioned and I wondered, but in my quest for knowledge, I brought a lot of things onto my plate as at this moment I have to try and set things straight. My power is returning ever so slowly and it is not to the point that I can do what I used to do before, but... will you help me, friend?"
Noah looked up at this being as his eyes shone sharply with curiosity and calculation.
"What exactly do you need help with?"
Anaximander smiled and stretched his hands as if testing the limits of his recovering existence.

"THE Early Veiled Shore of THE Creature," he said with weight behind every word. "I have to get back into it, and I need help in this as I do not know how much time we have. My actions brought about the result of many things, and Existence does not need to suffer because of me. Countless lifeforms do not need to suffer because of me. Please, help me right this wrong."
BOOM!
THE Early Veiled Shore of THE Creature?
Noah’s eyes shone luminously at such words as he got up from his seated position.

The First Farmer had mentioned a while ago that he heard a voice telling him to findTHE Early Veiled Shore of THE Creatureas a method to surviving The Fallout. At the time, Noah had filed that information away as something to investigate when the opportunity arose.

Noah did not particularly need this given his own preparations and the fortress he was building withTHE Infiniverse, but he was definitely interested in what secretsTHE Creature’spersonal Shore might hold.
So he looked toward the figure of Anaximander, this ridiculous oddity who defied the very laws of Existence through sheer declaration, and he said with a slight smile, "Just show me The Way."
WithinTHE Loom.

In a sea of vibrant paradox where contradictions bloomed like flowers in an impossible garden, a single entity was surrounded by paradoxical flames of Existence that burned without consuming and illuminated without revealing.
It was truly lonely at the top.

Very few could understand how those considered at the top felt because they had never climbed that high themselves. They had never made the sacrifices, the choices, and done everything that was required to reach such heights. They looked up at those who stood above them and saw only power and glory, never the cost that had been paid to acquire such things.
The struggles to get there were invisible to those who only saw the destination.
The sacrifices were forgotten by those who only celebrated the victories.
The choices, some of which haunted even the most powerful beings across eons, were unknown to those who had never been forced to make them.

Nobody understood whatTHE Living Paradoxhad to do to get where he was now, to even be capable of laying claim to The Oldest Paradox of Existence and stand as one of the few entities that could challenge the very foundations of reality itself.

But more often than not, beings like him who were at the top did not need others to understand because their drive and ambition was so unfathomably potent that they were a force to be reckoned with regardless of comprehension or sympathy.
Very few in Existence knew, butTHE Living Paradox was actually born a peasant.

An entity of low class who held nothing and had nothing, who scraped by in the earliest moments of his existence without power or authority or even the promise of either. But look at him now, surrounded by flames that embodied the very concept of contradiction, standing at the precipice of an act that would reshape all of Observable Existence.
The flaming figure of Paradox smiled briefly as memories of that humble beginning flickered through his ancient consciousness.

"I was born a peasant," he said with a voice that held both pride and a strange sort of acceptance."I will die a peasant. But in between... in between all of this, there will be immensity. There will be glory."
HUUM!
As he said this, he raised his hand and pointed above where the metaphorical clock representing Midnight hung in the paradoxical sky of his domain.
The massive hand moved from one second toward zero.
The time to Midnight was zero.

This was because he had sensed another one of his precautions being set off. He didn’t know which one of the myriad of things that he was careful of had been triggered, but he innately knew that something had tripped one of his countless safeguards scattered across Observable Existence. And it simply tipped the scales ever closer toward Midnight until there was nowhere left to tip.
As of this moment, there was no time between now and The Fallout.
What remained was preparations and activation.

At this moment,THE Living Paradoxactually raised his hand and saw his fingers trembling. His hand itself was actually trembling with minute vibrations that would have been invisible to anyone who wasn’t looking for them.
Was it out of anticipation or a sense of fear for what was to come?

His smile became brighter as his hand slowly stopped trembling, and it was a glorious sign of anticipation rather than dread. He was one of the few that knew how nothing would be the same after The Fallout transformed the landscape of Observable Existence.
The conditions that would allow for ascension to the higher Scales of Existence would bloom.
THE Creatureand many others would be set free from their various prisons and suppressions.
A free-for-all would unfold, but at a scale The Infinite Unfurling had never imagined and could never have prepared for.
The cards were set and nothing could be changed at this moment as Midnight approached. With the clock to Midnight hitting zero, The Fallout would unfold anywhere within the next few minutes or hours.

THE Living Paradoxmoved away from the sea of Paradox and appeared elsewhere withinTHE Loom, and before him a massive object burning with incandescent multicolored flames of Existence spun in the void. It looked like a cube, but it radiated such heat and majesty that even a Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty entity might be burned by its mere proximity.
THE Living Paradox appeared before it and stroked it with a nostalgic expression, his flaming hand passing over its surface with something approaching tenderness.

"Alright buddy, let’s do this," he said with a voice that held eons of preparation and anticipation. "Us against Existence. Let us change the landscape of Observable Existence. Let us have a sense of fairness out there where the strong have ruled unchallenged for far too long."
His voice grew harder, more resolute.

"Chaos? Existence? The First Tongue? Paradox? Fuck them. Fuck them all. Every aspect of The Oldest Paradox of Existence thinks they deserve to win, thinks they deserve to rule, thinks they deserve to define what reality is and what it should be."

As he finished saying these words, his eyes burned with a sense of immensity and veiled rage that had been building since the moment he first realized that Existence was unfair and that he had been born with nothing while others had been born with everything.
And then he moved forward, his hand reaching toward the burning cube that would initiate The Fallout and change Observable Existence forever.

sentences.text: He paused and looked at Noah with eyes that held centuries of gratitude for a being who had shown him kindness when he deserved none.
"I toldTHE Creatureto spread my Weavings out across Existence so that I could hide in fragments until the time was right," Anaximander continued.
"I set up new Guidelines to make it possible, declaring that my existence could be divided and scattered without diminishing my core self.
When a time in the future came when things settled down, a friend could come and wake me.
I thought that friend would beTHE Creaturereturning after his victory, but it turned out to be you."
He smiled with genuine warmth.
"So here we are, Friend."
Here they were.

Noah silently thought about everything he had just learned before he looked at Anaximander closely and asked the question that had been burning in his mind since he first encountered this impossible being.
"What is your Way?"
His Way.

Anaximander smiled at this question as he looked up to the endlessly obsidian ceiling above them, his expression one of peaceful contemplation as he considered how to explain something that defied conventional explanation.
"My Way is My Way,"he began with that familiar tone of a scientist trying to describe something beyond normal parameters.
"My Way is The Way.THE Creature called it The Way of THE Way when we discussed it during our conversations.
I called it just...
My Way.
The Way of Self."
He looked back at Noah with eyes that held the weight of profound understanding.
"You can call it another name if you wish, but it is simply a relationship between me and Existence," Anaximander continued.
"I tell Existence how things should be, and Existence simply needs to listen.
That is the Way.
That is my Way.
I do not fight against reality or bend it through force or authority.
I simply inform reality of how things are for me, and reality accepts my declaration as truth."
BOOM!
The Way of THE Way.
The Way of Self.

A power that allowed its wielder to redefine their relationship with Existence itself, to make declarations that reality was obligated to accept, to exist outside the normal parameters that bound evenTHEentities.
Noah looked at Anaximander with new understanding as the pieces fell into place.
This was whyTHE Living Paradoxwanted him destroyed so badly.
This was whyTHE Creaturemoved to protect him despite the betrayal.
This was why such a being had been hidden in fragments across Existence rather than allowed to remain whole.
Anaximander’s Way was a threat to the very order thatTHE Living Paradoxsought to impose through THE Loom and The Fallout.
Because how could you destroy someone who simply declared that they could not be destroyed?
How could you impose your will on someone who had already declared that external wills did not apply to them?
How could you win against someone who had decided that they had already won?
It was an absurd Way, and even with it, that bum, Paradox, had still won against it and Existence itself in their first clash.
Noah frowned as he thought about all of it!
As Noah thought about many things, Anaximander in front of him smiled as this being began to rise up on unsteady legs that grew stronger with each passing moment.
"I am an explorer," Anaximander said with that familiar tone of someone who had spent their entire existence chasing understanding.
"I am a scientist.
I questioned and I wondered, but in my quest for knowledge, I brought a lot of things onto my plate as at this moment I have to try and set things straight.
My power is returning ever so slowly and it is not to the point that I can do what I used to do before, but... will you help me, friend?"
Noah looked up at this being as his eyes shone sharply with curiosity and calculation.
"What exactly do you need help with?"
Anaximander smiled and stretched his hands as if testing the limits of his recovering existence.
"THE Early Veiled Shore of THE Creature," he said with weight behind every word.
"I have to get back into it, and I need help in this as I do not know how much time we have.
My actions brought about the result of many things, and Existence does not need to suffer because of me.
Countless lifeforms do not need to suffer because of me.
Please, help me right this wrong."
BOOM!
THE Early Veiled Shore of THE Creature?
Noah’s eyes shone luminously at such words as he got up from his seated position.
The First Farmer had mentioned a while ago that he heard a voice telling him to findTHE Early Veiled Shore of THE Creatureas a method to surviving The Fallout.
At the time, Noah had filed that information away as something to investigate when the opportunity arose.

Noah did not particularly need this given his own preparations and the fortress he was building withTHE Infiniverse, but he was definitely interested in what secretsTHE Creature’spersonal Shore might hold.
So he looked toward the figure of Anaximander, this ridiculous oddity who defied the very laws of Existence through sheer declaration, and he said with a slight smile, "Just show me The Way."
WithinTHE Loom.

In a sea of vibrant paradox where contradictions bloomed like flowers in an impossible garden, a single entity was surrounded by paradoxical flames of Existence that burned without consuming and illuminated without revealing.
It was truly lonely at the top.
Very few could understand how those considered at the top felt because they had never climbed that high themselves.
They had never made the sacrifices, the choices, and done everything that was required to reach such heights.
They looked up at those who stood above them and saw only power and glory, never the cost that had been paid to acquire such things.
The struggles to get there were invisible to those who only saw the destination.
The sacrifices were forgotten by those who only celebrated the victories.
The choices, some of which haunted even the most powerful beings across eons, were unknown to those who had never been forced to make them.

Nobody understood whatTHE Living Paradoxhad to do to get where he was now, to even be capable of laying claim to The Oldest Paradox of Existence and stand as one of the few entities that could challenge the very foundations of reality itself.

But more often than not, beings like him who were at the top did not need others to understand because their drive and ambition was so unfathomably potent that they were a force to be reckoned with regardless of comprehension or sympathy.
Very few in Existence knew, butTHE Living Paradox was actually born a peasant.
An entity of low class who held nothing and had nothing, who scraped by in the earliest moments of his existence without power or authority or even the promise of either.
But look at him now, surrounded by flames that embodied the very concept of contradiction, standing at the precipice of an act that would reshape all of Observable Existence.
The flaming figure of Paradox smiled briefly as memories of that humble beginning flickered through his ancient consciousness.
"I was born a peasant," he said with a voice that held both pride and a strange sort of acceptance."I will die a peasant.
But in between... in between all of this, there will be immensity.
There will be glory."
HUUM!
As he said this, he raised his hand and pointed above where the metaphorical clock representing Midnight hung in the paradoxical sky of his domain.
The massive hand moved from one second toward zero.
The time to Midnight was zero.
This was because he had sensed another one of his precautions being set off.

He didn’t know which one of the myriad of things that he was careful of had been triggered, but he innately knew that something had tripped one of his countless safeguards scattered across Observable Existence.
And it simply tipped the scales ever closer toward Midnight until there was nowhere left to tip.
As of this moment, there was no time between now and The Fallout.
What remained was preparations and activation.
At this moment,THE Living Paradoxactually raised his hand and saw his fingers trembling.
His hand itself was actually trembling with minute vibrations that would have been invisible to anyone who wasn’t looking for them.
Was it out of anticipation or a sense of fear for what was to come?
His smile became brighter as his hand slowly stopped trembling, and it was a glorious sign of anticipation rather than dread.
He was one of the few that knew how nothing would be the same after The Fallout transformed the landscape of Observable Existence.
The conditions that would allow for ascension to the higher Scales of Existence would bloom.
THE Creatureand many others would be set free from their various prisons and suppressions.
A free-for-all would unfold, but at a scale The Infinite Unfurling had never imagined and could never have prepared for.
The cards were set and nothing could be changed at this moment as Midnight approached.
With the clock to Midnight hitting zero, The Fallout would unfold anywhere within the next few minutes or hours.

chapters.title: Chapter 4668: Sanity and Greatness!
paragraphs: In the Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Infiniverse.
Alexander Asmodeus, The Peacemaker, stood while watching the emergence of Phonemes of The First Tongue far above him as they bloomed like celestial flowers across the blue-gold sky.
Osmont taught his people a language that nobody should be capable of grasping, and his people were shockingly grasping it.
Well, a very select few.

There was a Penguin that had begun getting hit by Osmont’s vibrant Goad after it seemed like the penguin was getting nowhere with its attempts at forming even the most basic Phoneme. The stick descended again and again with rhythmic precision, each strike accompanied by patient instruction that somehow made the violence seem educational.
But even that blue-gold stick in Osmont’s hands seemed to be hitting to infuse knowledge into the one being beaten as it seemed to be tough love of the most literal variety.
But either way...

|It’s a ridiculous thing is what it is. Is The First Tongue so easy to learn? Who the hell is this Osmont? And THE First Hunger and THE Living Origin being here... hey, I told you to talk to Origin before, why don’t you just step up? She and I have a debt...|

An incessant voice rang out in his head as it was an unfortunate byproduct of taking in the shattered part ofTHE Heart of Lawinto his existence. The voice ofTHE Living Lawwas now incessantly chirping whenever he chose to, which seemed to be constantly.
Alexander almost wanted to ask what he was supposed to be, he or she, as THE Living Existences and Law in particular seemed to take on whatever orientation suited them at any given moment.

|Hey, don’t talk shit about me. You know I can hear your thoughts now, right? I didn’t expect my heart fully joining you would make the Tool I refined eons ago react this way. And now... look, you’re doing better than even them.|

THE Living Lawhad their voice ring out in his mind as yes, something unexpected had happened when he declared his Way of Peace. The Enneagram had reacted heavily to the remnants ofTHE Living Lawas it was transforming into something he didn’t recognize, something that pulsed with authority far beyond what it had held before.

But at this moment, new Gems began to appear on the Enneagram that represented every single Phoneme of The First Tongue that Osmont taught above. Every Phoneme was inscribed as Osmont taught it, being analyzed by the Enneagram in real time, and he would be able to seamlessly voice and write out all 18 Phonemes within the next few minutes without even having to go through the grueling process of learning them traditionally.
It was a ridiculous capability to imagine as The Enneagram essentially allowed him to copy and utilize what others spent eons trying to master.

|Yeah, you really need to get a jump on it. As much as I adore that girl Seraphina, I need you to remove the other part of the Enneagram from her and fuse it together fully. Oh, and you can now sense remnants of my Collapsed Civilization, right? With the reaction of the Phonemes of The First Tongue and that, you grasping THE will now be easy as this Osmont really gave you a jumpstart. But you will need to get going. If The Fallout starts before you grasp those things... they will be gone forever.|
The incessant voice buzzed in his ears again as Alexander frowned at the implications of whatTHE Living Lawwas suggesting.

The remnants ofTHE Living Law’sCollapsed Civilization were scattered across Observable Existence, and if The Fallout consumed them before he could reach them, they would be lost forever along with whatever power and knowledge they contained. And the other part of The Enneagram that Seraphina carried needed to be reunited with his half to achieve its full potential.

He looked toward one of the nearby bodies of Osmont who was simultaneously teaching multiple groups of students with the efficiency of someone who had mastered the art of multitasking at an existential level. He thought about everything that was at stake and everything that could be gained if he moved now.
He looked at Seraphina and The Living Laws behind her, the manifestations of Law that had gathered in this Shore as refugees from a collapsing order, and he sighed as he called out to Osmont.
The Fallout neared, but he had to go out into danger rather than stay in this sanctuary that Osmont had built.

|Don’t worry, I am confident in your survival now. After all, I am in the end THE Living Law. Before Paradox collapsed me, I used to dine with Origin and THE Creature. I know the players in this game, and I know what it takes to survive them. With my guidance and your Way of Peace, we will carve out a place in whatever Existence looks like after The Fallout.|
They used to dine withTHE Creature and THE Living Origin, but why were they all doom and gloom days ago saying how it was such a shame, and if only Alexander had come across them earlier?

|Kid, I didn’t count on an anomaly giving you lessons on The First Tongue or helping you do the impossible by getting a Shattered Heart. All of that accelerated everything to impossible degrees. Now, all you need to do is finish the rest as with this, my Civilization will also undergo emergence much quicker. You win, I win. Mutual benefit.|
THE Living Lawremained incessant in his mind as Osmont arrived before him soon after.
The eyes of this terrifying anomaly alone were heavy to take, but Alexander took them on regardless as he began to talk!

Many people would take different paths across Existence as the apocalypse approached. Some would hide and hope to weather the storm. Some would fight and hope to overcome it. Some would flee and hope to outrun it.

At this moment, The Peacemaker was about to pioneer his own path, one that involved hunting down the remnants of a Collapsed Civilization while the very fabric of Observable Existence prepared to tear itself apart.
It was madness.
But then again, sanity had never been a prerequisite for greatness!

chapters.title: Chapter 4669: The Shore of THE Creature I
paragraphs: When the end of Existence was coming, what should one do?

Many across eons thought about this question endlessly, coming to conclusions that ranged from the profound to the absurd. Some argued that one should spend their final moments in contemplation, making peace with Existence and accepting the inevitable with grace and dignity.

Others suggested hedonism, indulging in every pleasure and desire before the void claimed everything. Still others advocated for connection, spending those precious remaining moments with loved ones and forging bonds that would transcend even annihilation.

There were those who chose denial, convincing themselves that the end was not truly coming and continuing their routines as if nothing had changed. There were those who chose despair, losing all hope and collapsing into nihilistic emptiness before the actual ending arrived.
And there were those who chose to end themselves before the end could claim them, preferring the illusion of control over the reality of helplessness.
All of these were valid responses to the incomprehensible weight of finality.
But Noah seemed to be taking an entirely different route.
He was going out sightseeing.

At this moment, he stood outside The Wandering Territories beyond his Infiniverse as beside him were the figures ofTHE Living Order, THE First Hunger, and THE Living Originwho could not stop looking at Anaximander with expressions ranging from curiosity to barely concealed shock.

Noah had just brought them out here as they looked at the figure of Anaximander who almost seemed malnourished, his form still recovering from eons of fragmented existence and the strain of being reassembled after so long scattered across Observable Existence.
And yet this maddening entity smiled toward them as he simply said, "Hello! Any friend of Osmont is a friend of mine. I am Anaximander."
He introduced himself casually as if they were meeting at a social gathering rather than on the eve of an apocalypse that would reshape all of Observable Existence.

Sigrid and THE First Hungerhad no immediate reaction beyond polite acknowledgment, but the eyes of Origin opened wide as if she had recognized that name and face from somewhere deep in her ancient memories.
She looked toward this being closely, evaluating him up and down as if trying to reconcile what she was seeing with what she remembered eons ago.
THE First Hungerlooked at Anaximander with curiosity while asking, "Are you like him?"
Tor asked this question while pointing toward Noah, and Anaximander couldn’t help but laugh at the comparison.
"Haha, no, my friend," he replied with genuine amusement dancing in his brilliant eyes. "Nobody is like this guy. He is something else entirely."

Noah looked at these interactions as he shook his head and said, "Anaximander, these are three THE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereignty entities who all have some connection to THE Creature. It would not be an issue to bring any of them, would it?"
Anaximander smiled as he considered the question.
"Not at all," he replied. "Although it might need to take a little bit longer because..."
As he spoke, he waved his hand, and without any fluctuation of energy or authority, a stick appeared in his grasp.
A stick that caused the faces ofTHE First Hunger and THE Living Originto pale as they recognized it right away.

This ancient-looking stick seemed to be made of a common tree, its surface worn smooth by countless hands over countless eons. And yet it emanated an air of terrifying might and majesty that belied its humble appearance.
It was none other than the stick ofTHE Creature. THE First Lesson.The stick thatTHE Creatureused to discipline Early Creatures back in the Earliest Folds!
BeforeTHE First Hunger and THE Living Origincould even ask where he had gotten the stick, Anaximander continued.

"This is going to open up the gateway that will bypass tedious travels of who knows how much distance," he explained while twirling the legendary stick casually. "And really, it isn’t even a matter of distance as much as... ah, it’s hard to explain. Distance didn’t matter toTHE Creature. The main thing is that I have been telling this stick to open up the way to The Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creature, but the power that I have recovered so far is only capable of allowing me to open it for you and I. I would have to wait a few more minutes in order to add a few more words to this Guideline to include these three others..."
Anaximander waved the stick around like it was nothing as Noah looked at it with shining eyes filled with curiosity and calculation.
Well, his stick was bigger as far as he could tell.

But this... hearing Anaximander talk about his Way made him curious as his eyes flickered with brilliance. A moment later, his eyes shone blue-gold as the Philology of Undifferentiated Mana bloomed around him in radiant patterns.
He floated closer to Anaximander and proceeded to touch his shoulder while sending out a glorious command internally.
’Utilize Way Manifestation to embody The Way of Anaximander.’
He actually proceeded to claim such a ridiculous thing as in the next moment...
|Warning: The target of the Way you have chosen to copy is an extremely complex one.|
|Analysis: The Way of Anaximander operates on principles that defy conventional replication.|
|Due to missing the anomalous factor unique to the user, The Undefined Way of Anaximander can be utilized in a limited fashion.|
|Duration: 10 seconds.|
|Capability: You have free reign to define Existence as you wish.|
|Cost: Your immensity will pay the price for each declaration.|
BOOM!
In the next moment, Noah’s eyes opened fully as he embodied The Way of Anaximander for the first time.

The sensation was unlike anything he had ever experienced before. There was a sense of freedom with it, a feeling that the rules of Existence were merely suggestions rather than laws. But it was also slightly unique and different from his own Way because where his Way worked with Mana and The First Tongue to shape reality, this Way simply... declared.

Around his body, the words of the terrifying Philology of Undifferentiated Mana buzzed with potent energy. Their presence causedTHE First Hunger and THE Living Originto look over once more, their eyes gradually opening as they began to recognize this Philology to be the one thatUl’Morethhad held in Ginnungagap all those eons ago!

Well, his stick was bigger as far as he could tell.
But this... hearing Anaximander talk about his Way made him curious as his eyes flickered with brilliance.
A moment later, his eyes shone blue-gold as the Philology of Undifferentiated Mana bloomed around him in radiant patterns.
He floated closer to Anaximander and proceeded to touch his shoulder while sending out a glorious command internally.
’Utilize Way Manifestation to embody The Way of Anaximander.’
He actually proceeded to claim such a ridiculous thing as in the next moment...
|Warning: The target of the Way you have chosen to copy is an extremely complex one.|
|Analysis: The Way of Anaximander operates on principles that defy conventional replication.|
|Due to missing the anomalous factor unique to the user, The Undefined Way of Anaximander can be utilized in a limited fashion.|
|Duration: 10 seconds.|
|Capability: You have free reign to define Existence as you wish.|
|Cost: Your immensity will pay the price for each declaration.|
BOOM!
In the next moment, Noah’s eyes opened fully as he embodied The Way of Anaximander for the first time.
The sensation was unlike anything he had ever experienced before.
There was a sense of freedom with it, a feeling that the rules of Existence were merely suggestions rather than laws.
But it was also slightly unique and different from his own Way because where his Way worked with Mana and The First Tongue to shape reality, this Way simply... declared.
Around his body, the words of the terrifying Philology of Undifferentiated Mana buzzed with potent energy.

Their presence causedTHE First Hunger and THE Living Originto look over once more, their eyes gradually opening as they began to recognize this Philology to be the one thatUl’Morethhad held in Ginnungagap all those eons ago!

chapters.title: Chapter 4670: The Shore of THE Creature II
paragraphs: As they looked toward Noah with mounting realization, he ignored everything while he said to Anaximander, "May I?"
He said such words while pointing to the stick ofTHE Creature, and Anaximander blinked in surprise before he nodded and gave the stick to Noah while saying, "Be careful, it is a little heavy."
HUUM!

The exchange ofTHE First Lesson of THE Creaturefrom one hand to another occurred as Noah felt a unique sense of immensity wrapping around his hands the moment his fingers closed around the ancient wood.
|You have grasped onto a Relic of History.|
|THE First Lesson has been held by your hands.|
|This artifact predates most of current Existence and has been used to shape the foundations of many civilizations.|
When Noah’s eyes flashed as he used Lens of Civilization on it...
|THE First Lesson|
|Classification: ???|
|Origin: ???|
|Creator:THE Creature|
|Power Level: ???|

|Description: The stick used byTHE Creatureto teach and discipline the earliest beings of Observable Existence. It has struck moreTHEentities than any other object in history. Its true capabilities remain unknown, asTHE Creaturenever revealed the full extent of whatTHE First Lessoncould accomplish.|
|Current Status: Dormant, awaiting its true wielder.|
Noah grasped it with sharp eyes as in the next moment he spoke out calmly, "This small stick will open up the way to The Early Veiled Shore of THE Creature for those of us floating here."
HUUM!

The sensation was ridiculously unique as he spoke while utilizing The Way of Anaximander. Every single word that he uttered felt extremely heavy, as if the immensity that he felt when he strung together Logos to form Philologies was what he was doing right now, but through pure declaration rather than linguistic construction.

But a moment later, the stick in his hand began to shine with multicolored brilliance as terrifyingly heavy and dense flames erupted from it. These flames proceeded to form into a multicolored doorway before them, its edges burning with authority!

The sense of heaviness that Noah felt was immense as all around him, many turned their eyes toward him with incredulity and shock. Only Sigrid remained calm, looking at the scene as if she was only watching something normal that her man was doing, her faith in him so absolute that even this seemed unremarkable.
Anaximander seemed purely amazed whileTHE Living Originwas actually somber while looking at him.
"Are you...truly sure that you are not THE Creature?" she asked with a voice that held genuine uncertainty.
Such words took Noah out of his stupor as he looked towardTHE Living Originand said firmly, "Let’s stop it with that. I am not THE Creature. I simply used The Way of Anaximander."
He simply used The Way of Anaximander.
Simply.
As if it truly was simple.
After he said this, he returned the stick ofTHE Creatureback to Anaximander as he felt the sense of heaviness in his existence after utilizing this unique Way.
He looked at the gateway that would lead to The Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creature, and before he entered, he uttered out with absolute certainty...
"My weight and immensity actually exceeds THE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty."
BOOM!

The moment that he uttered such words while utilizing The Way of Anaximander, he felt an immense sense of heaviness and weight as if he was lifting something so supremely heavy with a muscle he never knew he had.
The strain was unlike anything he had experienced before, as if reality itself was pushing back against his declaration while simultaneously being forced to accept it.
|Declaration Registered.|
|Cost Assessment: Extreme.|
|50% of all Infinite Potential that had been steadily flowing into your Foundation and Way has been instantly amplified and utilized.|
|Result: The immensity and weight of your Foundation has reached 10% the weight of a normal THE Intermediate Depth of Absolute Sovereignty entity.|

|Comparative Analysis: This is equivalent to 1% of the approximate weight of beings like THE Primordial Chaos, THE Living Paradox, or THE Creature when they were at THE Intermediate Depth of Absolute Sovereignty(Very, very rough estimate. In fact, may not even be accurate)|
|Your existence has been permanently elevated.|
The terrifying sensation of power that Noah felt was staggering as he sensed his Foundation settling into its new weight with authority that hadn’t been there moments before.
But then...
|Warning: The utilization of a Way without the proper anomalous factor has caused immense strain within your existence.|
|The manifestation of The Way of Anaximander has prematurely ended.|
|Cooldown before next manifestation: Unknown.|

The unique sensation of a muscle that he could not sense or explain being unfathomably tired faded away as he lost access to The Way of Anaximander. But he got a glimpse of just how this terrifying being operated, and this was enough for him to think about many possible things in the future regarding how such a Way could be studied, understood, and perhaps even partially replicated through his own methods.
His brazen words were heard by the others in the surroundings as Anaximander was looking at him with shining eyes filled with scientific curiosity.
Torsquinted while looking toward him before he shook his head and came up to wrap his right hand around Noah’s shoulder.

"Outsider, or The Scale Breaker as you were known in Ginnungagap," Torsaid with a tone that mixed admiration with gentle correction."It is good to dream, but you cannot dream out loud for everyone to hear. Even THE Intermediate Depth of Absolute Sovereignty takes some time to clear and go through. You cannot just say it out loud and expect to cross it and skip it entirely to go to THE Fundamental Depth. Come on, you have impressed us enough already. Let us go see The Early Veiled Shore of THE Creature."

Tor said this as if he were consoling him, but Noah merely shook his head asTHE First Hungerdid not realize that such a thing could actually be possible with the right circumstances and the right Way.
While motioning toward Anaximander to lead, the group made their way into the blazing multicolored flaming gateway, and they disappeared from the Wandering Territories.

All of them could instinctively feel that something was coming, and this whole interaction, all their words and exchanges, everything that they did here had taken thespan of less than a single second. After all, they were beings that could move faster than Planck Speed itself, and in even a nanosecond, many things could be accomplished.

The gateway closed behind them as they journeyed toward The Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creature, leaving the Wandering Territories empty and silent in the moments before The Fallout would change everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 4671: The Shore of THE Creature III
paragraphs: Existence was a mystery, but it was not necessarily a mystery that needed to be solved as much as it needed to be experienced.
Noah was experiencing it at this moment as he came across the glorious Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creature, a place that defied his expectations in ways he hadn’t anticipated.

Days ago such a place would not even have been a possibility for him to think of, but the Weavings of Existence changed very rapidly as he now found himself staring at an endlessly vast Shore that stretched beyond even his enhanced perception.
It was a weird thing to see as it felt like someone whothoughtthey were rich entering the home of someone that was truly rich.

Because The Early Veiled Shore of THECreaturewas a ridiculous one as the surroundings alone permeated with liquid and plasmic concentrations of Civilizational Authority that made even his own Infiniverse seem modest in comparison.

The golden sands they stood on were filled with thousands of Logos of The First Tongue just in the immediate proximity where they currently stood, each one a perfect expression of meaning that would take others eons to forge.

There were massive tall trees in the distance all around them that spanned upward infinitely, their canopies disappearing into heights that seemed to have no ceiling. Even these trees were swirling with hundreds of Logos of The First Tongue woven into their very bark and leaves, as the entire place emanated an air of immensity and sacredness that pressed down on visitors like a gentle but undeniable weight.
And just by taking a glance at the immediate surroundings,Noah was able to affirm that yeah, this place would be surviving The Fallout without question.
|Welcome to the Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creature.|
|In this place, the concentration of Logos and Philology of The First Tongue is so dense that the study of The First Tongue progresses 1,000 times faster than anywhere else in Observable Existence.|
|Warning: Be careful of what you touch, as you could trigger dangerous mechanisms left behind byTHE Creature.|

The entire place seemed wondrous as when they arrived, Sigrid stayed close to Noah whileTHE Living Originseemed dazed for a moment, as if she had returned to someplace she never thought she would see again. Her golden eyes were distant, filled with memories that stretched back to eras when this Shore had been alive with activity and purpose.
Moments later, she began to take steps toward a certain direction and rapidly disappeared in that direction without a word of explanation.
Tor shook his head and said calmly, "I’ll keep an eye on her..." as he also disappeared afterTHE Living Origin, leaving Noah, Sigrid, and Anaximander standing on the golden sands.

In front of Noah, the figure of Anaximander took the stick ofTHE Creatureas he began to draw a circle around them that shone brightly a moment later. Their figures were displaced vast distances across this Early Veiled Shore in an instant, traveling farther than light could travel in years.

They appeared in a region that held a golden cliff with a waterfall of golden sands filled with Logos flowing down toward a lower golden continent that stretched endlessly below. The sight was breathtaking in its impossible beauty, as even the falling sand seemed to sing with The First Tongue.
At the edge of the cliff, one could see a raised elevated stone-like platform that Anaximander began walking toward while carrying the stick with purposeful strides.

"The masses of Existence do not deserve to be unraveled and faced with immense anguish," Anaximander said with conviction as he approached the platform. "THE Creatureleft a few things in place, and at this moment I will use the remaining power of his Early Veiled Shore to draw in any forms of life across Observable Existence into this place. All Wheels of Existence, all Folds, every single form of life shall be contained in the Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creatureas at the time of The Fallout, this place shall serve as refuge."
He paused and looked back at Noah with those brilliant, curious eyes.

"The idea of distance and vastness does not truly apply to it as even with all of Observable Existence compressed into it, at most it would cover half of this space. And this is the main Shore ofTHE Creature, as I believe there are other parts of it that were shattered in his battle which are scattered across Observable Existence. It’s actually a very interesting place thatTHE Creaturemanaged to cultivate. Most of his time was spent here from what he told me."
The Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creaturewas utterly insane to grasp as Noah wondered what he would be able to find here during his exploration.

He watched as Anaximander went toward the elevated golden stone-like platform and raised the stick of THE Creature in his hands. Shockingly, he plugged it into the platform as if it were a key fitting into a lock that had been waiting eons for this moment.

A moment later, the entire region they were in began to vibrate as auroras of colors began to shine brilliantly above them in patterns that seemed to tell stories in a language older than The First Tongue itself.

Noah looked up and saw a terrifying formation of Logos begin to flow across the golden sands of this place, and even more began to float across the skies as they looked like rivers of brilliance streaming in all directions.

The Logos he could see were related to movement and displacement. Logos of Gathering that pulled things toward a central point. Logos of Compression that made vast spaces fit into smaller ones. Logos of Protection that wrapped around everything being drawn in. Logos of Preservation that ensured nothing would be damaged in transit. All of them working in harmony to accomplish what Anaximander was doing in order to displace countless life forms across Existence into this place.

As such waves of brilliance began to radiate all around, in the far distance at least a gigaparsec away, Noah began to see thousands of Transcendent Wheels of Existence begin to manifest in the skies as if they were plucked out of wherever they were and brought here. In other directions, entire Folds began to manifest as the skies or the ground opened up and began extending in all directions to accommodate the incoming refugees.
|Process Initiated: Existential Evacuation Protocol.|
|THE Creature’scontingency plan for catastrophic events has been activated.|
|All life forms across Observable Existence are being drawn into the Early Veiled Shore.|
|Estimated coverage: 100% of Observable Existence.|
|Estimated time to completion: Approximately 60 seconds.|
|This process will drain significant reserves of the Shore’s accumulated authority.|

As the process began, the figure of Anaximander continued to hold on to the stick as if it was a key that was directing everything. He looked toward Noah and Sigrid with a smile that held both exhaustion and satisfaction.

"This might take a little bit... well, maybe a minute or so to cover all of Observable Existence since I am going in a bit of a hurry due to not knowing when The Fallout will descend," he said. "But you guys can take the time to look around the home ofTHE Creature.I was amazed the first time that I got here and studied everything that I saw."
Noah nodded at these words.
"We’ll stay close by,"he replied. "Let us know if you need anything."

After such words, Noah looked out to the vibrant expanse of The Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creature,and he began to float up as one of the first things he saw was a vast and endlessly stretching wooden wall that seemed to be breaking down and decaying in places.
His eyes focused on it with sharp curiosity.
|Structure Identified: The Veil of Existence.|
|Classification: Primordial Barrier.|
|Function: Separates The Lands of The Living and The Lands of The Dead.|
|History:THE Creatureestablished this barrier with the help of Anaximander in an era beforeTHE Loomwas conceived.|
|Current Status: Worn down and breaking apart due to eons of attacks, strain, and the absence ofTHE Creature’smaintenance.|
Noah looked at this radiant wall that was breaking apart as he shook his head at the implications of what its deterioration meant.
At this time, Sigrid beside him sighed as she also observed the crumbling barrier.

"Even someone as powerful as this, who had a place like this, was not able to come out on top and win over conflicts eons ago,"she said with a voice that held both wonder and melancholy. "And the biggest conflict for us, which we did not know whether we could survive or not, already had a solution right here. We were fighting with everything that we had to be able to survive The Fallout, when there was an answer that we could not access waiting in this place all along."
Noah listened to her calmly as they moved rapidly across the Shore, and he took her hand into his as he considered her words carefully before responding.

"Sometimes a problem seems impossible, but there’s always an answer out there," he said with certainty. "Sometimes one just does not know how to access it. The solutions to surviving The Fallout could be countless, but one simply has to find the right answer among all of them. We found our own answer without needing to rely on another, and that matters more than you might think."
He paused as they continued moving through the golden landscape.

"Because relying on others can sometimes backfire," he continued. "If we simply sat back and held the hopes that THE Creature would save all of Observable Existence, we could all have perished. Who would have saved Anaximander if we hadn’t found him? No, relying on others is never ideal in Existence as the best possible solution is to rely on oneself. Rely on yourself and every success and failure will be your responsibility."
At such words, Sigrid smiled and hugged his hand closer to her as she looked up at him with eyes that held absolute devotion.

"I want to rely on you," she said softly. "Even if it is inadvisable to rely on others. Can I continue to put my life in your hands? If you succeed, I’ll be there with you. If you fail, I will shoulder that failure with you."
At such words, Noah turned to her and stroked her head gently with his free hand.
"Yeah, continue relying on me," he said with a confident smile. "I am pretty reliable so far."

After such words, Sigrid smiled brilliantly as their figures continued moving across The Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creature, with Noah intent on exploring to see if he could find anything useful for the current him in this place.

They were doing all of this in the span of femtoseconds and nanoseconds as all around them in the vastness of the Shore that was gigaparsecs in size, Wheels of Existence and Folds began to bloom and appear. Entire regions of the Wandering Territories were being brought over into The Early Veiled Shore ofTHE Creatureas the allure of Collapsed Civilizations also began to flow into this place.

When it did come to Collapsed Civilizations, history was not entirely clear on how the events had unfolded with all of THE Living Existences. The fates of THE Living Dimensional, THE Living Quantum, THE Living Concept, THE Living Spirit, or Temporal were unique and shrouded in mystery. Some were within THE Loom, some may have been collapsed entirely, and some may have found other fates that no one had recorded.
When the dust settled after The Fallout, everything would be clear.
